title: Deterministic CUDA graph recapture for concurrent multi-stream decoding
creator: Miranda Park
description:
Problem: In multi-stream decoding we attempt to capture CUDA graphs for the prefill + steady-state decode paths to reduce per-token overhead, but recaptures are non-deterministic when concurrent streams mutate shared allocator state, temporaries, or the KV cache layout. This causes subtle replay mismatches (wrong attention offsets, corrupted KV pointers) and intermittent correctness failures in production.

Goal: Implement a deterministic recapture workflow and guardrails so that CUDA graph reuse is correct across concurrent streams with dynamic sequence lengths and attention-key/value memory growth. Maintain performance benefits of graph replay while preventing silent correctness regressions.

Scope: Focus on the runtime path that: (1) performs prefill capture (full-sequence prefill that initialises KV cache), (2) replays graphs for per-token decode across multiple CUDA streams concurrently, and (3) interacts with kernel selection heuristics (fused attention / flash kernels) and allocator behaviour. Does not include model-level operator reimplementation.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic reproduce of a previously observed correctness failure is eliminated on the repro harness (no mismatches after 1000 randomized concurrent sessions)
Prefill capture logic consistently snapshots KV memory layout and allocator state so replay on a different stream does not corrupt pointers or attention offsets
End-to-end latency and p50/p95 token cost regressions are <5% compared to current baseline when graphs are used; if graphs are disabled fallback path must meet existing SLOs
Automated CI tests covering variable sequence lengths, dynamic memory growth, and mixed kernel selection (flash vs fallback) added and green
Deployment toggles exist for canarying graph recapture heuristics as runtime flags and a metric is emitted when a recapture occurs (with reason tag)
implementation_notes: Introduce a per-capture capture_context object that records allocator checkpoints (free lists offsets) and kv-cache base offsets as opaque integers to be validated at replay time
Serialize dynamic kernel selection decisions used during capture (kernel IDs + config like block sizes) and validate on replay; if mismatch -> safe fallback to immediate-launch path
Pin capture to an abstracted memory arena when possible during prefill: pre-allocate a stable KV slab sized for the session to avoid eviction-induced pointer shifts
Use cudaStreamWaitEvent and explicit event barriers to order capture->replay transitions across streams; avoid relying on implicit stream semantics
Add a short-lived capture-mode allocator which disables coalescing and defragmentation during capture to preserve pointer stability; revert after capture finishes
Add instrumentation hooks to dump graph-capture metadata (sha256) to perf logs for offline correlation with failures
test_plan: Unit: allocator checkpoint/restore fuzz tests that simulate concurrent allocations and verify pointer stability across checkpoint boundaries
Integration: multi-stream decode harness (internal tool) that runs 2000 sessions with variable seq-lens and kernel mixes; assert token-output equality against CPU reference
Load: ramp to 10x typical concurrent sessions on staging to detect race windows in capture/recapture under pressure
Regression: add CI job that runs a deterministic seed variant of the harness on PRs touching the capture code
Chaos: introduce artificial delays in stream events and allocation paths to validate fallback heuristics
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_deterministic_recapture` (off by default)
Canary: enable for 1% of hosted traffic routed to a small dedicated pool; monitor correctness metric and per-token failure rate
Gradual rollout to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks if no regressions
Auto-disable policy: if correctness failures > 0.01% or latency regression beyond threshold observed, flip flag off and collect traces for debugging
risks: Performance regressions if deterministic allocator constraints increase fragmentation or force memcpy of KV slabs
Complexity: more state to serialize/validate increases attack surface for bugs and may complicate future kernel autotuning
Edge cases where kernel selection differs between capture and replay (driver changes or nightly kernel bundles) will force fallbacks, reducing benefit
Incorrectly scoped capture_context could leak memory or be stale, creating new classes of nondeterminism
